title: Surjectivity of henselian restriction for bounded abelian coefficients
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with $X=\operatorname{Spec} A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and quotient-induced map $i:Z\to X$. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\acute et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], killed by multiplication by an integer $n>0$. For every $q\geq0$ the canonical restriction $H^q(X,G)\to H^q(Z,i^{-1}G)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is surjective. The statement has no arbitrary coefficient-ring module structure and asserts only surjectivity.

source.place: Tags 09ZE, 09ZH and 09ZI, proofs; finite Z/n coefficient case

proof.text: Identify the quotient immersion image with V(I). Apply henselian Stein connectedness and the finite-connected-intersection criterion to obtain bijective abelian global sections; conjugate by the degree-zero section/cohomology identifications. This is the degree-zero proof already in Gabber.lean, reused without a cyclic import.
Induct on the degree, uniformly for sheaves killed by the fixed n, applying the finite-coefficient successor step to the preceding-degree bijectivity hypothesis. Retain surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09ZH degree-zero argument; induction using the finite Z/n coefficient successor step from Tags 09ZE and 09ZI
